techniques.name: Focus ring: pop on click, trim to point
techniques.summary: A thin outline around a control either pops outward and fades the moment it is clicked, or draws itself clockwise around a target and erases from the tail, pointing at the action without a cursor.
techniques.recipe: Draw an SVG rounded rect around the control's bounds, with rx equal to the control radius plus the outset, a crisp 2-3 px stroke and no blur copy. Pop mode: on the press frame, grow the outset from 4 to 14 px with prog(..., E.out) over 8 f and fade the stroke from 0.9 to 0 linearly over 20 f. For a handoff, keep the ring at 14 px instead so it becomes the border of the next element (an alert card, or the frame of the next shot). Trim mode: 6 px outset, dasharray '10 8', masked by a second rect with pathLength 1 that shows only the run from tail to head (strokeDasharray `${h - t} 1`, strokeDashoffset -t). Here head = prog(f, s, s + 24, E.smooth) and tail = prog(f, s + 24, s + 48, E.smooth). Repeat on the next target about 108 f later while the cursor rests nearby. Use C.accent for the stroke only when the accent's one meaning is 'act here'; otherwise use C.ink on light stages and C.white on dark ones.
techniques.timing: Pop: outset 4 to 14 px in 8 f E.out; opacity 0.9 to 0 over 20 f, linear from the press. Trim: draw 24 f and erase 24 f, both E.smooth (a 48 f loop); dashes 10/8 px, 3 px stroke; next target about 108 f later.
techniques.use_when: A click needs a visible result the next shot can build on, or a calm frame must point at the next action without moving a cursor.
techniques.avoid_when: The cursor already sits on the target (the ring is redundant), or the ring would need a glow or blurred halo to read.

techniques.name: In-place character rewrite
techniques.summary: A small monospace status field is overwritten left to right by its new state, or a sensitive value turns to dots and deletes from the right, all inside the same fixed slot with no layout change.
techniques.recipe: Set the field in FONT.mono with whiteSpace pre so every character keeps its column. Overwrite: k = fd(prog(f, s, s + 12, E.linear) * max(oldLen, newLen)) and text = next.slice(0, k) + prev.slice(k). Start it 8 f into the press release, so the status changes as the button's light fades. Optionally lift a companion icon 10 px over 4 f E.out and bring it back over 8 f. Redact: on the click frame, swap the value to '•'.repeat(n) in one frame, then set n = len - fd((f - s) / 2) so one dot deletes every 2 f. Meanwhile, an anchor-camera pan over 40 f E.inOut keeps the toggle icon centred; put the click on a downbeat.
techniques.timing: Overwrite at about 1 character per frame (13 characters in 12 f), linear, starting 8 f after the press peak. Redact: 1 f swap, then 1 dot deleted every 2 f; camera pan 40 f E.inOut.
techniques.use_when: The product's own status (sending, receiving, connected) or a privacy claim should change in place and read as the machine's voice.
techniques.avoid_when: The text is decorative rather than real UI status (it becomes filler text), or the field uses a proportional face, so the columns jump.

techniques.name: Anticipation dip before an unlock
techniques.summary: Light builds on a locked card, the card briefly darkens as the lock's shackle swings open, then it pops to clean full-tone content, so the release feels bigger than it is.
techniques.recipe: Drive the card wrapper's filter brightness through a tw chain: 1.0 to 1.5 over 14 f E.in (the build), then 1.5 to 0.8 over 12 f E.out (the dip). On the pop frame, swap the locked art for the clean art in one frame (decided with fd), hidden inside the brightness pulse, never crossfading the two. Set brightness to 1 + 0.35 * hitPulse(t, 3, 6) and scale to 1 + 0.024 * hitPulse(t, 4, 4): a pulse, not a spring. During the dip, rotate the shackle -30 degrees about its hinge (transformOrigin at the hinge point) with E.out and lift it 4 px. Repeat it faster on a second card (a 7 f pop instead of 12 f) so the second read is snappier, and put a 'pop' or 'snap' event on each pop frame.
techniques.timing: Build 14 f E.in to 1.5x. Dip 12 f E.out to 0.8x, with the shackle at -30 degrees. Pop 12 f (7 f on the repeat) with a hitPulse(t, 3, 6) brightness pulse and a 2.4% scale pulse. About 38 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Something locked, gated or hidden becomes available (an unlock, a reveal, access granted) and the moment should land as a payoff.
techniques.avoid_when: The brightness would clip whites into a bloom, or the film already has two big payoff beats.

techniques.name: One-element tell before the event
techniques.summary: Just before a state change or a cut, exactly one small thing moves, such as a plus glyph turning 45 degrees into an x or an object slowly turning toward its target, while everything else holds.
techniques.recipe: Plus mode: rotate the plus glyph 0 to 45 degrees with prog(f, cut - 16, cut - 6, E.smooth) so it finishes 6 f before the cut. Repeat it before every result cut so the viewer learns the tell. Yaw mode: rotateY the object 0 to 35 degrees over 40 f E.linear inside perspective 1200px. The camera tail creeps at most 0.1% scale per frame and nothing else changes; fire the event (a 2-4 f impact or a hard state change) on the frame the yaw ends. The tell is the motion of the shot, so keep it to one element and add no cursor.
techniques.timing: Plus: 10 f E.smooth, finishing 6 f before the cut. Yaw: 40 f linear to 35 degrees, with the event on the next frame; camera creep at most 0.1% per frame.
techniques.use_when: A repeated result cut, or a sudden 2-4 f event, needs anticipation so it reads as caused rather than random.
techniques.avoid_when: Several things already move in the frame (the tell gets lost), or the yaw would leave the rest of the frame static for more than 48 f.

techniques.name: Chip bloom around content
techniques.summary: A container grows out of its content: a dropped icon tile widens into a labelled chip that floods with the accent and wipes back to an outline, or a solid pill swells behind a name so the group becomes a button.
techniques.recipe: Tile to chip: on the drop, scale the tile 0.8 to 1 over 8 f E.out. Then tween the pill width from the tile width (equal to its height) to the label width plus padding over 12 f E.out. On the same progress, the icon slides to its left slot and the label reveals with a clip-path inset from the right. A flat C.accent fill clipped to the pill is erased by a mask-image linear-gradient with an 80 px feather, sliding left to right over 20 f E.outSoft and leaving a 1.5 px border. Bloom behind: an absolutely positioned pill behind the text (radius height/2, C.ink fill) tweens from the text bounds (measureTracked) to the bounds plus 48 px on each side over 10 f E.out. Meanwhile the text mixes from C.ink to C.white over 6 f, starting on the bloom's second frame. Hold the finished chip at least 18 f before it does anything else.
techniques.timing: Tile pop 8 f E.out; widen 12 f E.out; fill wipe-off 20 f E.outSoft with an 80 px feather; bloom behind 10 f E.out with a 6 f text inversion; hold at least 18 f.
techniques.use_when: An integration, tag or name should become a tangible, clickable object (attached, added, now a button), shown as cause and effect.
techniques.avoid_when: The fill would need several hues to read, or the chip has nothing to do next (a bloom with no follow-up reads as decoration).

techniques.name: Shape handoff: pill becomes the icon
techniques.summary: A labelled capsule empties its text, then collapses at a fixed height into a square tile or circle that becomes the next thing (the app icon, a loader or a dock slot), so the object never disappears, it changes role.
techniques.recipe: One div owns the shape and tweens width, height and borderRadius, with its content centred. Empty the label first. Either backspace from the end (one character every 1-2 f, with fd) or delete from both ends at once (text.slice(k, n - k), k + 1 every 5 f), with the pill width hugging the measured text plus padding over 8 f E.out per step. Then collapse the width down to the height about the centre over max(40, e/7) f on E.inOut, where e is each edge's travel in px (half the width lost), so each edge peaks under about 55 px/f (E.inOut peaks at 7.7x its mean speed). Take the radius from 999 to 22% of the side for a tile, or to 50% for a circle. Then do one of three things: loop a 3x3 pixel-dot loader inside it (one dot step every 6 f); raise an arrow glyph into the circle through overflow hidden (translateY 100% to 0 over 14 f E.out); or tween the tile to a dock-slot rect over 20 f E.out while the dock mounts behind it and sibling icons scale in on SPR.micro at a 6 f stagger. Close with a 1 + 0.05 * hitPulse(t, 3, 5) scale pulse just before the cut.
techniques.timing: Backspace 1 character every 1-2 f (pairs every 5 f, width hug 8 f E.out). Collapse max(40, edge travel / 7) f on E.inOut at a fixed height (each edge under about 55 px/f). Dock variant 20 f E.out plus SPR.micro siblings at 6 f. The loader holds about 72 f.
techniques.use_when: A thinking state, prompt or button should hand off to the product identity, or to its new place in the interface, in one continuous take.
techniques.avoid_when: The target shape has nothing to do with the source (the continuity feels arbitrary), or the shot needs a hard cut for rhythm.

techniques.name: Guide cursor: arrive, hover, press
techniques.summary: A cursor travels a bowed path to the element about to act, the target shows its hover state a few frames after the cursor arrives, and a short press triggers the response on the same frame.
techniques.recipe: Use src/fx/Cursor.tsx in screen space: position = cursorArc(from, to, prog(f, m0, m1, E.smooth), 0.2), with the target from toScreen(shot, point), and press = pressAt(f, CLICK). The target's response (a press envelope or a state flip) starts on CLICK. Calm mode: travel at 5-15 px/f along the path and arrive 6-12 f before the press. The target's hover fill (C.mist, or a 6% ink tint) fades in over 4 f, starting 4 f after arrival, and any highlight that follows the cursor trails it by 4 f. Snappy mode, for vertical or phone-size frames: scale the cursor to about 11% of frame height (Cursor scale about 2.8 at 1080p). Move about 300 px in 24 f with E.out (about 72 px/f on the first frame, velocity x0.78 per frame), then dwell about 60 f while the UI reacts. Once the product acts on its own, fade the cursor out over 10 f after its last click.
techniques.timing: Calm: arcs at 5-15 px/f on E.smooth, bow 0.15-0.25, arriving 6-12 f early; hover starts 4 f after arrival and takes 4 f. Press: 4 f down, 8 f recoil (pressAt). Snappy: 300 px in 24 f E.out, dwell about 60 f. At most one click per 30 f, at uneven gaps; exit fade 10 f.
techniques.use_when: A person is driving the product, and dense UI needs a point of view that shows the viewer where to look next.
techniques.avoid_when: The product acts on its own, clicks would come faster than one per 30 f, or the shot already has a pointer such as a focus ring.

techniques.name: Velocity-stretch dot
techniques.summary: A small round dot (a cursor or a list marker) stretches into a capsule along its motion in proportion to its speed, anchored at its trailing end, and shrinks back to a dot when it stops.
techniques.recipe: Compute the head H(f) from an eased path, clamped to its start position before the move. Compute the tail as a pure-function exponential follow: T(f) is the sum over i = 0..29 of 0.8^i * H(f - i), divided by the sum of 0.8^i, which gives a lag of about 4 f. Draw an SVG line from T to H with strokeLinecap round, strokeWidth equal to the dot diameter, a flat fill and no shadow. Size it at 3.3-5.3% of frame height for a cursor (C.white on dark), or 18-21 px for a list marker (C.accent). Marker mode: drop it in from the top edge over 31 f E.out, so it arrives as a long streak that shortens into the dot. Hop it 54 px to the next item over 22 f E.smooth on a 54 f cadence, with the active label mixing from C.mute to C.ink over 8 f around the hop midpoint. Exit by stretching it into a dash about four times the dot's length (about 84 px for a 21 px marker) over 17 f on E.smooth, then shoot it off with E.in. The stretch is the streak, so draw nothing behind it.
techniques.timing: Tail weights 0.8^i over 30 f (a lag of about 4 f): length about rest + 4-5.5 f x speed, back to a dot in 16-20 f. Marker: drop 31 f E.out; hop 54 px in 22 f E.smooth every 54 f; label colour 8 f; exit: stretch to an ~84 px dash over 17 f (E.smooth), then off on E.in.
techniques.use_when: A tiny element must lead the eye across a slab or down a list, and needs speed, direction and character.
techniques.avoid_when: UI truth requires a standard system arrow, or several dots would stretch at once (the trick only reads once).

techniques.name: Shared highlight walks the menu
techniques.summary: One rounded highlight slides from row to row of a sidebar or menu, trailing the cursor, and the chosen row settles into a pale accent tint.
techniques.recipe: Render a single absolutely positioned highlight behind the rows: radius 8 px or row height / 2, C.white on a dark sidebar, C.mist on a light one. Tween its translateY and height to each target row's rect, taken from the layout data, over 12 f E.out, starting 4 f after the cursor reaches that row. Walk about 24 f per row; the first hover can appear in one frame. On the click, mix the chosen row's background to C.accent at 10% opacity over 8 f E.ui and its label to C.ink, then fade the moving highlight over 8 f. The row text never moves.
techniques.timing: 12 f E.out per hop; about 24 f per row; trails the cursor by 4 f; click tint 8 f E.ui; highlight fade 8 f.
techniques.use_when: Navigation through a menu, sidebar or list should read as a small human decision, with spatial continuity.
techniques.avoid_when: The rows are too small to read at the shot's framing (push in first), or a soft radial bloom would be added to the highlight.

techniques.name: Stretchy tab indicator
techniques.summary: The selected pill of a segmented control shoots to the new option with its leading edge arriving first, stretches to about 1.9x its width mid-travel, then hugs the new label as the label takes the active colour.
techniques.recipe: Animate the indicator's leading and trailing edges as two tweens on the same E.glide: the leading edge reaches the target edge in 12 f and the trailing edge in 20 f. Width = right - left therefore swells to about 1.9x near frame 6 and relaxes into the target width. Keep the height fixed, the radius at height / 2 and the fill flat. Mix the new label from C.mute to the active colour over the last 8 f, and the old label back over the first 8 f. Step the new label's weight from 500 to 600 on the landing frame with fd. Calm variant: fade the fill to a 1.5 px outline ring over the first 6 f. Swell the ring to 1.35x by 30% of the travel and shrink it onto the target by 100%, over 48 f E.smooth, then snap the solid fill back over 4 f on landing. Put a tick on the landing frame.
techniques.timing: Leading edge 12 f, trailing edge 20 f, both E.glide, for hops up to about 250 px. For longer hops keep the 0.6 ratio and lengthen both so the leading edge stays under about 65 px/f (a 420 px hop takes 18 f / 30 f). Label colour 8 f. Calm variant: 48 f E.smooth, 6 f fill fade, 4 f snap.
techniques.use_when: A tab, filter or toggle switch causes the next state (the chart changes, the list swaps) and deserves weight.
techniques.avoid_when: The control has more than about five options in a tight row (the stretch overlaps its neighbours), or the indicator would only read with refraction or a frosted backdrop behind it.

techniques.name: Radial dash burst around a word
techniques.summary: Short dashes burst outward around a hero word on the beat, drift almost imperceptibly while it is read, then fly outward faster as the frame pushes into the cut.
techniques.recipe: Place 22 rounded rects (4x20 px) around the word at angles from rand(`dash${i}`), oriented radially, in C.ink at 60-80% opacity. Their radius is r = 187 + 87 * prog(f, b, b + 16, E.out) + 0.5 * max(0, f - b - 16), plus 176 * prog(f, cut - 20, cut, E.in) in the last 20 f while the camera pushes in. The motion-blur pass smears the burst and the exit. Start it on the beat the word lands.
techniques.timing: Burst +87 px in 16 f E.out; drift 0.5 px/f for about 50 f; exit +176 px over the last 20 f E.in into the cut.
techniques.use_when: A single hero word on a beat needs a physical punch.
techniques.avoid_when: The text is body copy, the shot is UI, or the burst has already been used once in the film.
techniques.ban_safe_variant: Replace the random dashes with 12 evenly spaced radial ticks (every 30 degrees, 20 px long, 3 px stroke, C.ink, one SVG) forming an ordered ring around the word. Drive them with the same radius curve: 187 to 274 px in 16 f E.out, a 0.5 px/f drift, then out to about 450 px over the last 20 f E.in. It reads as a graphic emphasis mark rather than debris. A single 2 px ring stroke on the same curve also works.

techniques.name: Launch hop that never lands
techniques.summary: A centred app icon hops up as if launching, hangs at the top for a beat and starts to fall, and the camera leaves before it lands, so the hop motivates the scene change.
techniques.recipe: Chain the icon's translateY with tw: 0 to -77 px over 10 f E.outSoft, hold 4 f, then -77 to +20 px over 18 f E.contact (gravity, ending with velocity), with no squash. Scale a soft contact shadow from 1 to 0.85 and fade it as the icon rises. Start the scene change (a camera tilt-away, a whip or a cut) on frame 14, the first frame of the fall, so the landing never resolves on screen.
techniques.timing: Rise 77 px in 10 f E.outSoft; hold 4 f at the top; fall 18 f E.contact; the camera leaves from frame 14; 32 f in all.
techniques.use_when: Opening the app or launching a feature should motivate the move to the next scene with a familiar OS gesture.
techniques.avoid_when: The icon must come to rest in the same shot (then it needs a real landing), or several icons would hop in turn.

techniques.name: Two-beat confirm cascade
techniques.summary: A row of buttons or toggles confirms one by one: the label or knob changes first, the fill follows a beat later, and the rows go at uneven, human gaps.
techniques.recipe: Give the rows irregular start frames, never a metronome: for example [0, 4, 19, 37] for four toggles, or [0, 10] for two buttons. Button: swap the label at t0, with a 4 f crossfade or a 6 f roll (the old label rises 8 px and leaves, the new one enters from 8 px below through arrive()). Then mix the background from C.ink2 to C.accent over 8 f E.out, starting at t0 + 12. Toggle: slide the knob 0 to 20 px over 8 f E.out with no overshoot, and mix the track from C.line to C.accent over 10 f E.smooth from the same frame. Put a light 'tick' (weight 0.25-0.35, panned by x) on each state change.
techniques.timing: Label 4-6 f; fill 8 f E.out at +12 f. Knob 8 f E.out; track 10 f E.smooth. Row gaps such as 4, 15 and 18 f.
techniques.use_when: Several integrations, permissions or capabilities switch on, and each confirmation must stay legible at video speed.
techniques.avoid_when: There is only one control (use the press envelope), or every row would start at the same interval.

techniques.name: Spinner resolves to a check
techniques.summary: A working indicator (a rotating dashed ring in a step list, or a small spinning disc pushed into the middle of a sentence) turns into a check with a short tag the moment the step is done.
techniques.recipe: Working: an SVG circle (r 10-12 px, 2.5 px stroke, dasharray '4 4' or a 270-degree arc) rotated (f - s) * 7.5 degrees, one turn per 48 f. Inline variant: open a slot between two words by tweening its width 0 to 1.4em over 6 f E.out (the words slide apart as flex siblings). In it, spin a 1.2em x 0.6em accent disc with a 3 px C.ink rim on rotateX, one turn per 24 f linear, in perspective 300px. Done: on the done frame (fd), replace the spinner with a check ring that draws strokeDashoffset 1 to 0 (pathLength 1) while scaling 0.6 to 1 over 8 f E.out. The tick path draws over 8 f from 3 f later, a small 'Done' tag rises 6 px and fades in over 8 f, and the step label mixes from C.mute to C.ink. Start the next step's spinner on that same frame, and put a pitched 'pop' on each check's 50% frame, climbing with each step.
techniques.timing: Ring: one turn per 48 f, linear (disc: one per 24 f). Slot opens over 6 f E.out. Check ring 8 f E.out from 0.6; tick draws over 8 f from +3 f; tag 8 f. One step every 24-36 f.
techniques.use_when: The product works through steps on its own (an agent, a sync, an import), and each completion should land as a small lock.
techniques.avoid_when: There is a single long wait with nothing resolving (show progress instead), or all the checks would resolve on one frame.

techniques.name: Send as a ghosted handoff
techniques.summary: On send, the composer's text drifts up and fades away while the same content appears above as a posted message, briefly overlapping the old text, instead of flying between containers.
techniques.recipe: From the send press, fade the composer text over 12 f using q = prog(f, send, send + 12, E.smooth): opacity 1 - q, translateY -12 * depart(q) px, and blur blurOut(q, 4), so it only softens once it is moving. Starting 4 f after the press, bring the posted bubble in at its final place over 18 f, with opacity on E.smooth and translateY 12 to 0 px through arrive(prog(..., E.out)). Empty the composer on frame +12 and bring its placeholder back over 8 f. Pair it with the press envelope on the send button.
techniques.timing: Composer out over 12 f E.smooth (-12 px, blur up to 4 px). Bubble in over 18 f from +4 f (12 to 0 px, E.out with arrive). 8 f of overlap; placeholder back over 8 f.
techniques.use_when: A message, prompt or post is submitted and the result appears elsewhere in the same frame; this is calmer and cheaper than a flight.
techniques.avoid_when: The journey itself is the point (show the flight), or the move would serve as a transition between shots, where a crossfade is never the default.

techniques.name: Drag, lift and seat
techniques.summary: A chip or file picked up by the cursor lifts off the surface, follows the hand with a slight lag and tilt, then drops into its slot with a small contact squash as the slot accepts it.
techniques.recipe: On the grab (pressAt), scale the item 1 to 1.04 and deepen its shadow from 0 2px 4px to 0 16px 32px at 18% black over 8 f E.out. While dragging, place it at the cursor path evaluated at f - 3 (a 3 f lag). Tilt it by rotateZ = clamp(vx * 0.25, -6, 6) degrees, where vx is the cursor's horizontal speed. When it enters the slot, thicken the slot outline from 1 to 2 px and tint it over 6 f E.ui. On release, run the last 40-80 px into the slot on E.contact over 8 f and settle the scale and shadow back. Apply squash(t) anchored at the contact edge, and put a 'snap' or light 'land' on the contact frame.
techniques.timing: Lift 8 f E.out to 1.04 with a 16/32 px shadow. Follow lag 3 f; tilt at most 6 degrees. Slot tint 6 f E.ui. Drop 8 f E.contact, plus squash over about 8 f.
techniques.use_when: A drag-and-drop (attach a file, add an integration, reorder a card) causes the next state.
techniques.avoid_when: The drag path is long (over about 600 px, cut it), or the item contains text that must be read while it tilts.

techniques.name: Badge count bump
techniques.summary: A notification badge or counter chip ticks up: the digit rolls to the next value while the badge gives a small pulse, once per increment.
techniques.recipe: Draw the badge as a pill (C.accent fill, C.white tabular-nums digit) with the digit in an overflow-hidden slot. On each increment frame c, roll the old digit up and out and the new one in from below, one line height of travel over 8 f, with arrive(prog(f, c, c + 8, E.out)). Pulse the badge scale to 1 + 0.12 * hitPulse(f - c, 2, 5), and retween its width over 8 f E.out when the digit count changes (9 to 10). The badge first appears from its icon's corner (transformOrigin there) on SPR.micro. Space increments unevenly, at least 12 f apart, with a 'tick' of weight 0.3 on each.
techniques.timing: Digit roll 8 f E.out; pulse hitPulse(t, 2, 5) x 0.12; width 8 f E.out; first appearance on SPR.micro; increments at least 12 f apart, uneven.
techniques.use_when: Incoming activity (messages, leads, approvals) should register as small, countable events on the UI.
techniques.avoid_when: The count is the hero number of the shot (use a full counter), or increments would come faster than about one per 12 f.

techniques.name: Click to focus: I-beam, ring, caret
techniques.summary: An arrow cursor turns into an I-beam as it enters an empty field and clicks. The field's border sharpens, a caret appears and blinks twice at an uneven, human pace, and on the first key the placeholder vanishes and the pointer fades away.
techniques.recipe: Draw the I-beam as a variant of src/fx/Cursor.tsx: a 2.5 px C.ink stem 28 px tall with 9 px crossbars over a 2 px C.white outline, using the arrow's drop shadow. Its stem centre, not a tip, sits on the hotspot, and it scales about that point. The arrow travels on cursorArc and swaps to the I-beam in one frame, on the fd(f) where its tip enters the field's rect, arriving 8-12 f before CLICK. On CLICK (pressAt) the field takes focus: its border goes from 1.5 px C.line to 2 px C.ink through mixColor on prog(f, CLICK - 1, CLICK + 4, E.ui), so the change shows on the press frame, with no halo. On the same frame a 0.08 em x 1 em caret appears at the start of the text, while the C.mute placeholder stays where it is. Blink the caret on a hard, uneven table decided with fd: on 18, off 16, on 24, off 12 f, then the first key at CLICK + 70 (or just on 18, off 16 when the beat is tight). The pause should read as a person gathering a thought, never as a metronome. On the first key the placeholder vanishes in one frame, TypeOn takes over with a solid caret, and the I-beam fades out over 8 f on E.smooth, because a system pointer hides while typing. Run one log-space push toward the field under the arrival and the blinks (lc between two shots in src/lib/camera.ts, up to about 1.8x over 40-44 f on E.cam), so the wait is never a still frame. Put one 'click' at weight 0.3 on CLICK and no sound on the blinks.
techniques.timing: Arrive in 24-36 f on E.smooth, 8-12 f before the click; glyph swap 1 f; press 4 f down, 8 f recoil; focus border 5 f E.ui from CLICK - 1; caret blink in hard steps of 18/16/24/12 f (70 f) or 18/16 f (34 f); placeholder gone in 1 f on the first key; I-beam fade 8 f E.smooth; push up to 1.8x over 40-44 f E.cam.
techniques.use_when: A shot opens on an empty prompt, search or chat field and the first action is typing into it, so the click into the field becomes the cause of everything after.
techniques.avoid_when: The field is already focused or pre-filled, the product acts on its own with no cursor, or the film has already played the full two-blink wait once (later prompts start at the first key).

techniques.name: Cursor glyph follows context
techniques.summary: The pointer changes shape with what it is over, as a real system pointer does: an I-beam over text, an open hand over something draggable, a closed fist while dragging, and the arrow everywhere else. Each change is a one-frame swap.
techniques.recipe: Add a kind prop to src/fx/Cursor.tsx ('arrow' | 'ibeam' | 'hand' | 'grab'). Draw every glyph with the same C.ink fill, 2.4 px C.white outline and drop shadow, and give each its own hotspot, so a swap never shifts the point the cursor acts on: the arrow keeps its tip at (x, y); the I-beam (a 2.5 px stem 28 px tall with 9 px crossbars) is centred on (x, y); the open and closed hands have the hotspot at the centre of the hand. Choose the kind on fd(f) from the layout rects, never by tween. Use 'ibeam' while the hotspot is inside a text field or selectable text, 'hand' over a draggable item, and 'grab' from the frame pressAt goes down on a grab until the release. Then show 'hand' for 6-10 f until the hotspot leaves the item, and 'arrow' everywhere else. Each swap takes one frame, with no crossfade or scale blend. The press scale (1 - 0.12 x press) and the motion-blur pass apply to every glyph alike, and the fist appears on the press frame, so closing the hand is the press. While dragging, evaluate the item's path at f - 2 so it rides behind the fist and reads as pulled. Use the I-beam only on slow approaches (15 px/f or less) and at no less than about 2.2% of frame height (Cursor scale about 1.6 at 1080p), because its thin stem flickers in fast motion.
techniques.timing: Swap in 1 f on the frame the hotspot crosses a rect edge; fist on the pressAt down stroke (4 f down, 8 f recoil); open hand for 6-10 f after the release; item trails the fist by 1-3 f; I-beam approaches at 15 px/f or less.
techniques.use_when: A cursor drives a walkthrough that both types and drags, and the pointer must behave like the real system's rather than an arrow stamped on everything.
techniques.avoid_when: The cursor only clicks buttons (the arrow is correct there), or a snappy vertical edit would flash the glyph changes past before they read.

techniques.name: Drag-select snaps glyph by glyph
techniques.summary: An I-beam presses at the start of a phrase and drags across it, a tinted highlight grows behind the text one whole character at a time, and on release a small action bar grows out of the selection, ready for the product to act on it.
techniques.recipe: Measure the line once under FontGate: px[k] = measureTracked(text.slice(0, k), size, weight, track) for every k, so the highlight snaps to real glyph edges. Park the I-beam on boundary a and press with pressAt at DOWN. Then drag it to boundary b along x = lineLeft + mix(px[a], px[b], prog(f, DOWN + 2, DOWN + 2 + D, E.smooth)), with D = max(24, 2 x (b - a)) f, so the cursor stays at or under 12 px/f. The selection end is the boundary nearest the cursor, decided on fd(f): k is the index in a..b that minimises |px[k] - x|. The highlight therefore jumps one glyph at a time and never tweens, and that stepping is what makes it read as a real selection. Draw it between the field and the glyphs (layer order: field, highlight, text, cursor), from px[a] to px[k] at full line height with a 3 px radius, in mixColor(C.paper, C.accent, 0.22), keeping the text C.ink. On a dark stage use solid C.accent with C.white text, but only if the accent means 'chosen'. Release the press 6 f after the last step. 4 f later, grow an action bar 12 px above the line from the selection's top centre: transformOrigin at its bottom centre, scale lmix(0.05, 1, prog(f, UP + 4, UP + 14, E.out)), opacity over its first 4 f. For the follow-up, either remove the range in one frame (highlight and glyphs together, with the rest of the line closing up through the measured layout) and type the replacement in from px[a] with TypeOn, or restyle the selected glyphs in place. To select a whole word, use a double click: two presses 8 f apart select it in one step on the second press.
techniques.timing: Drag about 2 f per glyph (24-40 f) on E.smooth, cursor at 12 px/f or less; highlight steps per glyph on whole frames; release 6 f after the last step; action bar 10 f E.out from +4 f; hold at least 36 f before the edit; replacement typed over about 26 f; double-click presses 8 f apart.
techniques.use_when: The product acts on a piece of text the user picks (rewrite, translate, comment, format, ask about a passage), and the pick should read as a human choice rather than a preset.
techniques.avoid_when: The text is under about 40 px tall at the shot's framing (push in first), the range spans more than two lines, or the cursor never touches text anywhere else in the film.
